rules.message: Field "Addresses" (json: "addresses") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Annotations" (json: "annotations") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Domain" (json: "domain") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Enabled" (json: "enabled") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Service" (json: "service") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "SourceRanges" (json: "sourceRanges") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Type" (json: "type") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "ExternalDNS" (json: "externalDns") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "PrefixTemplate" (json: "prefixTemplate") in ExternalApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.

"gateway" has no doc comment of its own, so the CRD reference and kubectl explain publish type `GatewayExternalConfigApplyConfiguration`'s comment under it: "GatewayExternalConfigApplyConfiguration represents a declarative configuration of the Gate". That opens with the Go type name, which users never type - they type "gateway". Add a comment on the field; it takes precedence over the type's.
Field "Enabled" (json: "enabled") in GatewayExternalConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "ParentRefs" (json: "parentRefs") in GatewayExternalConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "AdvertisedPort" (json: "advertisedPort") in GatewayExternalConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Group" (json: "group") in GatewayParentRefConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Kind" (json: "kind") in GatewayParentRefConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Name" (json: "name") in GatewayParentRefConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "Namespace" (json: "namespace") in GatewayParentRefConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.
Field "SectionName" (json: "sectionName") in GatewayParentRefConfigApplyConfiguration has no doc comment. It ships blank in the CRD reference and in kubectl explain.

context.name: listeners.kafka
context.string: Kafka API listeners.

context.name: listeners.kafka.external.default.type
context.string: External access type for this listener. Unset inherits the cluster-wide external.type (NodePort/LoadBalancer). Set to "tlsroute" to route this listener via Gateway API (requires external.gateway above): a bootstrap + per-broker TLSRoute is created and the listener is excluded from the NodePort/LoadBalancer service. Other listeners can stay on the conventional type, enabling gradual migration.

context.name: external
context.string: External access settings. For details, see the [Networking and Connectivity documentation](https://docs.redpanda.com/docs/manage/kubernetes/networking/networking-and-connectivity/).

context.name: external.type
context.string: External access type. Only `NodePort` and `LoadBalancer` are supported. If undefined, then advertised listeners will be configured in Redpanda, but the helm chart will not create a Service. You must create a Service manually. Warning: If you use LoadBalancers, you will likely experience higher latency and increased packet loss. NodePort is recommended in cases where latency is a priority.

context.name: external.gateway
context.string: Gateway API TLSRoute-based external access (alternative to NodePort/LoadBalancer). The chart creates a bootstrap TLSRoute plus one per-broker TLSRoute, routed by SNI through a Gateway you manage. Opt individual listeners in by setting their type: `listeners.<service>.external.<name>.type: tlsroute` (see listeners.kafka.external below). The Gateway itself is NOT created by the chart; reference it via parentRefs.

context.string: Listener settings. Override global settings configured above for individual listeners. For details, see the [listeners documentation](https://docs.redpanda.com/docs/manage/kubernetes/networking/configure-listeners/).

context.name: addresses
context.string: Specifies addresses for the external listeners to advertise.Provide one entry for each broker in order of StatefulSet replicas. context.name: domain
context.string: Specifies the domain to advertise to external clients. If specified, then it will be appended to the `external.addresses` values as each broker's advertised address.

context.name: prefixTemplate
context.string:
Specifies the template used for generating the advertised addresses of
Services. This field accepts a string template that dynamically
constructs Service addresses based on various parameters such as Service
name and port number.
For historical backwards compatibility, this field is present on both
internal and external listeners. However, it is ignored when specified
on internal listeners.
